newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-GEBRSELASSIE CONFIDENT TRACK WILL BE WATERED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GEBRSELASSIE CONFIDENT TRACK WILL BE WATERED.

text.p: Ethiopian Olympic 10,000 metres champion Haile Gebrselassie said on Sunday he was confident that the world championships track here could be watered in order to make it softer.

"It's very easy to put water on the track and I don't see why they wouldn't do it," said Gebrselassie, who withdrew from the 5,000 metres race in Atlanta because he had sustained blisters from the track when winning the 10,000.
International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) general secretary Istvan Gyulai said the issue would be studied by the event's technical delegates.
"I am not aware of any rule stating water should not be put on the track," he said.

Gebrselassie, who will defend his 10,000 metres title here, said he understood the sprinters' need for a hard track but thought the demands of the long distance runners for a softer surface should also be taken into consideration.
"I think tracks should suit both the sprinters and the long distance runners and I hope that will be the case in the future," he said.
"Many people told me before I came here that the track was very much like the one in Atlanta and that's why I asked for water to be put on it."
A number of athletes here have commented on the hard surface.
Ato Boldon of Trinidad demonstrated that it suited the sprinters by equalling the fourth fastest time in history when he clocked 9.87 seconds in his 100 metres second round heat on Saturday.
Gyulai said the track confirmed to IAAF specifications.
"This track is not irregular at all," said Gyulai. "It corresponds fully to the parameters set by IAAF."
